sentences.text: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rahul Bharti, Judge

Three claim petitions were born out of one accident which occurred on 03.08.2009 involving offending vehicle (bus) bearing registration no. JK02E-6137 bearing the appellant as being its registered owner.
Said three claim petitions came to be disposed of by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, MACT, Kathua resulted in passing of a common award dated 11.11.2016.

3.

Thus, the total compensation payable in relation to the aforesaid three cases comes to Rs.
8,81,000/-.

4. The admitted fact of this case is that the offending vehicle was being plied without insurance cover and that has resulted in the onus of payment of compensation resting securely on the shoulders of the appellant as being the registered owner notwithstanding his plea that the appellant had transferred the offending vehicle to the current owner.

5. For the purpose of maintaining the present three appeals, the appellant has made the statutory deposit totalling to Rs. 75,000/- meaning thereby out of total compensation of an amount of Rs.
8,81,000/- exclusive of the interest, the appellant has paid Rs. 75,000/- as a deposit before this Court.
c/

w 6. The claimants have not received a single penny of the aforesaid compensation amount except the compensation under section 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 during the stage of adjudication of the claim petition.
It would be travesty of justice in case this Court insists the claimants/respondents to bear the present litigation without getting even single penny out of compensation paid to them.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant urges before this Court to make an effort for an amicable settlement of the matter with the claimants.

8. Expecting response to this plea of the appellant, the bonafide of the appellant must first come on board and for that purpose let him deposit an amount of Rs. 5,00,000/- (five lacs) with the Registrar Judicial of this Court within a period of one month.
9. Needful be done by the next date of hearing, otherwise, the present appeal would be heard on merits subject to risk and cost of the appellant.
